+The 64 bit register `vsacecrstatus` tracks the configuration and dirtiness of CRs on a per-CR basis.
+The `vsacecrstatus` register exists only when the H extension is implemented.
 
+``vsacecrstatus[``2__i__+1,2__i__``]`` can take the values Off, Initial, Clean, and Dirty, as defined for `vsstatus.ACES`, for CR #__i__.
 
-//
+When XLEN=32, `vsacecrstatush` is a 32-bit register that aliases bits 63:32 of `vsacecrstatus`.
+Register `vsacecrstatush` does not exist when XLEN=64.
+
+When V=1, `vsacecrstatus` substitutes for the usual `sacecrstatus`, so
+instructions that normally read or modify `sacecrstatus` actually access
+`vsacecrstatus` instead.
+
+When V=1, attempts to execute any ACE instruction that accesses CR #__i__ raise
+an illegal-instruction exception when ``vsacecrstatus[``2__i__+1,2__i__``]`` is
+set to Off.
+
+When V=1 and ``vsacecrstatus[``2__i__+1,2__i__``]`` is set to Initial or Clean,
+executing any instruction that changes CR #__i__ will change
+``vsacecrstatus[``2__i__+1,2__i__``]`` to Dirty.
+// TODO: ace.reset and ace.clear should set Initial
+
+Implementations may also change ``vsacecrstatus[``2__i__+1,2__i__``]`` from
+Initial or Clean to Dirty at any time, even when there is no change in CR #__i__ state.
+
+NOTE: `sstatus.ACES`, `vsstatus.ACES`, and `sacecrstatus` are also in effect when V=1.
+
+NOTE: Future extensions might define a `macecrstatus` register that would allow
+M-mode to optimize context switches of Supervisor domains.
+// `uacecrstatus` might become useful when the HFI extension lands, but that is
+// pushing the concept
